# 1. KV Caches: The Core Memory Structure

### Mechanism
During autoregressive generation, LLMs predict the next token by computing the hidden states of earlier tokens. Computing these states from scratch at every step requires re-processing the entire prompt—an operation with $O(N)$ complexity per step, where $N$ is prompt/sequence length.

To avoid this, inference engines maintain an intermediate cache known as the **Key-Value (KV) Cache**:
* At step $t$, the model computes embeddings $q_t, k_t, v_t$ for the newly generated token.
* The previous keys and values $\{k_1, \dots, k_{t-1}\}$ and $\{v_1, \dots, v_{t-1}\}$ are retained in the KV cache.

# 1. KV Cache: The Foundation of Generative Inference

### Concept & Mechanics
Autoregressive language models calculate the probability of the next token based on all preceding tokens:
$$P(w_t \mid w_1, w_2, \dots, w_{t-1}) = \text{Softmax}(W_Q W_K^T) \cdot W_V$$

Without caching, computing logits for step $t$ requires re-processing the entire sequence from token $1$ to $t-1$ at every generation step. This causes compute costs to scale quadratically $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ with sequence length $N$.

# 1. KV Caches: The Core Memory Engine

### Mechanism
During autoregressive generation, LLMs predict the next token by conditioning on all previously generated tokens. Mathematically, the forward pass computes Key ($K$) and Value ($V$) vectors for each token. Storing these per-token vectors in memory avoids recomputing past representations when generating token $t+1$. This stored state is the **Key-Value (KV) Cache**.

For layer $l$ with sequence length $S$, model hidden dimension $d$, and total layers $L$:
$$\text{KV Cache Size per layer} = 2 \times S \times d \times b \quad (\text{in elements, where } b \text{ is bytes per element})$$
$$\text{Total KV Cache} = L \times 2 \times S \times d \times b$$
